name: Michael Dell
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Dell Technologies; founder of DFO Management (family office)
profile: Founded Dell from his UT Austin dorm room in 1984; took it private with Silver Lake in 2013, bought EMC for $60B in 2016 and relisted in 2018. Dell is now a major AI-server supplier. Much of his fortune sits in family office DFO Management (hotels, credit); in 2025 he and his wife pledged $6.25B to seed savings accounts for 25M U.S. children.
interesting_fact: At 19 he was selling upgraded PCs out of his UT Austin dorm room, grossing about $80,000 by the end of his freshman year.
deep_cut_fact: His first job, at about 12, was in a Chinese restaurant in Houston: he started washing dishes, was 'promoted' to water boy, then assistant maitre d'; at 14 he worked at a stamp-and-coin store assessing gold and silver people brought in to sell.
notes: Very active on X (@MichaelDell) and talks often about AI infrastructure; best formal route is Dell Global PR (media relations). Strong fit for data-center/AI-factory topics.

name: Jen-Hsun Huang
current_role: Co-founder, President and CEO, Nvidia
profile: Taiwan-born engineer (Oregon State, Stanford MSEE) who worked at AMD and LSI Logic before co-founding Nvidia in 1993. He has run it ever since, steering it from PC graphics chips to CUDA and the GPUs that power AI data centers, making Nvidia one of the world's most valuable companies. Now pitches 'AI factories' and sovereign AI to governments and hyperscalers.
interesting_fact: Nvidia was conceived in a booth at a Denny's in San Jose in 1993; as a teenager Huang had worked at Denny's as a dishwasher, busboy and waiter.
deep_cut_fact: He was a serious junior table-tennis player: he scrubbed floors at Portland's Paddle Palace club to pay for tournaments, and at 15 finished third in junior doubles at the U.S. Open Table Tennis Championships.
notes: No personal social accounts; all requests route through Nvidia corporate communications. Extremely high-demand; frames everything around 'AI factories' and data-center power, a natural podcast fit. Name commonly given as Jensen Huang.

name: Warren Buffett
current_role: Chairman emeritus and director, Berkshire Hathaway (stepped down as CEO end-2025 and as chairman Sept 2026)
profile: The 'Oracle of Omaha' built Berkshire Hathaway from a failing textile mill into a ~$1T conglomerate (insurance, BNSF, Berkshire Hathaway Energy, big Apple/BofA/Occidental stakes). Greg Abel became CEO on Jan 1, 2026; in Sept 2026, at 96, Buffett became chairman emeritus as son Howard took the chair. He has given away ~$66B of stock since 2006.
interesting_fact: He filed his first tax return in 1944 at age 14, reporting $592.50 of income (mostly from a paper route) and deducting $35 for his bicycle and $10 for watch repair as business expenses; he paid $7 in tax.
deep_cut_fact: Terrified of public speaking, he signed up for a $100 Dale Carnegie course, stopped the check, then re-enrolled paying cash so he'd have to show up. His Columbia degree isn't on his office wall, but the Carnegie certificate (dated 1952) is.
notes: Berkshire has no press office/PR firm or published press email; Buffett historically answers by letter to his Omaha office (address on berkshirehathaway.com). X account is verified but essentially inactive. Now 96 and stepping back (chairman emeritus since Sept 2026) - podcast odds very low; Berkshire Hathaway Energy (Abel's former unit) is the energy angle.

name: Larry Ellison
current_role: Executive Chairman and Chief Technology Officer, Oracle Corporation
profile: Cofounded Oracle (as Software Development Laboratories) in 1977 and ran it as CEO for 37 years before becoming executive chairman/CTO in 2014; owns roughly 40% of the company. Oracle's AI cloud/data-center boom made him the second person ever worth $400B+ (Sept 2025). Also owns ~50% of Paramount Skydance, most of Lanai, and funds the Ellison Institute of Technology in Oxford.
interesting_fact: He never finished college and started out building databases for the CIA; the CIA project's codename at Ampex, 'Oracle', later became the company's name.
deep_cut_fact: He sailed as a crew member aboard the trimaran USA 17 in the deciding race of the 2010 America's Cup in Valencia; ESPN noted he and tactician John Kostecki were the only Americans on BMW Oracle's crew for the clincher.
notes: Press email is Oracle Corporate Communications (Deborah Hellinger), as listed on Oracle's Oct 2026 Investor Day release. Ellison rarely does outside interviews; Oracle earnings calls/Investor Day are where he speaks publicly. Strong data-center/AI-infrastructure fit (OCI, Stargate).

name: Jensen Huang
current_role: Co-founder, President and CEO, NVIDIA
profile: Taiwan-born engineer who cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and has run it since, taking it public in 1999. Nvidia's GPUs went from gaming to the backbone of AI data centers, pushing its market cap past $4 trillion in 2025; Huang owns roughly 3%. He has funded engineering centers at Stanford ($30M) and Oregon State ($50M).
interesting_fact: After arriving in the US, his aunt and uncle sent him to a rural Kentucky boarding school for troubled youth, mistaking it for a prep school; he cleaned the boys' bathroom daily. He later waited tables at Denny's, which he says cured his shyness.
deep_cut_fact: As a teen he was a nationally ranked table-tennis player: in a Jan 1978 letter to Sports Illustrated, Paddle Palace owner Lou Bochenski called him 'perhaps the most promising junior ever to play table tennis in the Northwest', noting he scrubbed the club's floors to pay for tournaments.
notes: Extremely high-demand; route via NVIDIA Corporate Communications. Does not run personal social accounts of note.

name: Zeng Yuqun
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd (CATL); vice chairman, All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce
profile: Robin Zeng (b. 1968, Ningde, Fujian) co-founded consumer-battery maker ATL in 1999, stayed on after TDK bought it in 2005, then spun out its EV-battery unit as CATL. CATL listed in Shenzhen in 2018 (Hong Kong 2025) and is the world's largest EV-battery maker, now pushing into grid energy storage, sodium-ion cells and battery swapping.
interesting_fact: He holds a PhD in condensed matter physics from the Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, earned in 2006 while already running ATL.
deep_cut_fact: Before batteries, the marine-engineering graduate of Shanghai Jiao Tong University started out at a state-owned shipbuilding company in Fujian, then spent about 10 years at an electronic-parts factory (SAE Magnetics, part of TDK) before co-founding ATL with two former colleagues.
notes: No published press/IR email found on catl.com in this pass (site has a Contact Us section). Best route is CATL's corporate communications via catl.com; English name Robin Zeng.

name: Liang Wenfeng
current_role: Founder and CEO, DeepSeek (Hangzhou); co-founder of quant hedge fund High-Flyer
profile: Liang Wenfeng (b. 1985) co-founded quant fund High-Flyer in 2015-16 with Zhejiang University classmates, using AI-driven trading to build one of China's largest quant firms and a large GPU cluster. He spun that compute into DeepSeek in 2023; its low-cost R1 model (2025) shook the AI industry. DeepSeek raised $7.4B in June 2026 at a $52B valuation.
interesting_fact: While still a student, DJI founder Frank Wang (Wang Tao) reportedly invited him to join DJI as a co-founder; he declined to pursue AI in financial markets. He met President Xi Jinping at a 2025 tech-entrepreneur symposium in Beijing.
deep_cut_fact: His 2010 Zhejiang University master's thesis was on object tracking with low-cost pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) cameras, supervised by Xiang Zhiyu; the work appeared as 'Algorithm of robust object tracking using PTZ camera' (Liang Wen-feng & Xiang Zhi-yu) in the Journal of Zhejiang University (Engineering Science), 2011.
notes: Extremely media-shy; DeepSeek has historically declined press requests and Liang has given only a couple of interviews (e.g. 36Kr/Waves, translated by ChinaTalk). service@deepseek.com is a general company contact, not a press desk. Company-level X account only; no personal social accounts.

name: Robin Zeng
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. (CATL); vice chairman, All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce
profile: Zeng (曾毓群) co-founded ATL in 1999 making lithium-polymer batteries for gadgets; after TDK bought ATL in 2005 he spun its EV-battery unit out as CATL in 2011. CATL, based in his hometown Ningde, is the world's largest EV-battery maker (Shenzhen/HK-listed), supplies BMW, Geely and Tesla, and is expanding into grid storage.
interesting_fact: Early in his career he worked at a state-owned shipbuilding company in Fujian; he studied marine engineering at Shanghai Jiao Tong University before moving into electronics and batteries.
deep_cut_fact: He kept studying while building ATL: an MSc in electronics/information engineering from South China University of Technology (2001), then a PhD in physics from the Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (2006) - a battery tycoon with a physics doctorate.
notes: Rarely gives Western media interviews; no personal social accounts found. Best route is CATL IR/corporate communications. Strong fit for energy-storage and EV-battery topics; note US geopolitical sensitivity around CATL.

name: Andreas von Bechtolsheim
current_role: Founder and Chief Architect, Arista Networks (leads advanced AI, silicon and optics initiatives)
profile: German-born engineer who co-founded Sun Microsystems in 1982 after building the original SUN workstation as a Stanford grad student. Wrote an early $100,000 check to Google, and in 2004 co-founded Arista Networks, now a key supplier of Ethernet switching for AI data centers; he owns a large stake and focuses on AI networking, silicon and optics.
interesting_fact: He built the original SUN (Stanford University Network) workstation as a grad student; Sun Microsystems was named after it. He has co-founded two other networking firms with David Cheriton (Granite Systems, sold to Cisco; Kealia, sold to Sun).
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager in a Lake Constance village (~1973) he built an Intel 8080-based controller for a local CNC-machine maker, coding it in binary on a hex keypad with no assembler. Too young to be hired, he was paid a royalty per box sold, and soon out-earned his teacher father.
notes: No personal social accounts found; best route is Arista corporate communications (Amanda Jaramillo). He speaks at OFC/Optica events on AI optics, a good hook. Under a 2024 SEC settlement he cannot serve as a public-company officer/director for five years; avoid the topic. Jugend forscht national physics winner 1974.

name: Len Blavatnik
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Access Industries (owner of Warner Music Group stake, LyondellBasell, DAZN)
profile: Soviet-born US/UK investor who emigrated in 1978, studied at Columbia and Harvard Business School, and made an early fortune via TNK-BP (stake sold in 2013 for $7B). His Access Industries bought Warner Music in 2011 for $3.3B and holds stakes in LyondellBasell, DAZN, biotech and tech (incl. DigitalOcean). Has given/pledged over $1B, mostly to universities.
interesting_fact: He bought Damien Hirst's gilded woolly mammoth skeleton 'Gone (but) Not Forgotten' for $15M in 2014, and has produced Broadway shows including 'The Front Page' and 'Sunset Boulevard'.
deep_cut_fact: His first US job was as a computer programmer in the biostatistics department of Mount Sinai School of Medicine; the pay let him study computer science at Columbia part-time. He then worked at Arthur Andersen and Macy's, and applied only to Harvard Business School ('I was pretty naive').

public_contacts.value: AccessIndustries@HawthornAdvisors.com (Hawthorn Advisors, all Access Industries press inquiries)

notes: Rarely gives interviews; best route is Hawthorn Advisors (Access press agency). Blavatnik Family Foundation also linked from Access site. Data-center angle: Access holds a stake in DigitalOcean.

name: Henry Samueli
current_role: Cofounder and director, Broadcom Inc. (stepped down as chairman June 2026); owner of the NHL Anaheim Ducks; chairman, Samueli Foundation
profile: Electrical engineer and former UCLA professor who cofounded Broadcom with Henry Nicholas in 1991 in a Redondo Beach condo; Broadcom's broadband and networking chips (now central to AI data-center networking and custom AI accelerators) made him a billionaire. He stepped down as Broadcom chairman in June 2026 but remains a director, and focuses on the Ducks, Honda Center/OCVIBE and the Samueli Foundation.
interesting_fact: Son of Polish Holocaust survivors, he holds 75+ patents and won the Marconi Prize; he and his wife gave UC Irvine $200M in 2017, the largest gift in the school's history.
deep_cut_fact: In 7th grade he talked his teacher into letting him build a five-tube radio kit (a ninth-grade project) instead of a crystal set; decades later he tracked down the same kit, a Graymark 506B, on eBay and built it again.
notes: No personal social accounts found. Samueli Foundation (Corona del Mar, CA; info@samueli.org) is the most personal route; Broadcom corporate comms for chip/AI topics. IEEE Spectrum's 2025 Medal of Honor profile is a great prep read. Deep-cut source is IEEE (accessible).

name: Vagit Alekperov
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder of Lukoil (president 1993-2022; left the board in April 2022)
profile: Baku-born oilman who worked Siberian fields at Surgutneftegaz and Kogalymneftegaz, became the USSR's youngest deputy oil and gas minister in 1990, then built Lukoil from Langepas-Uray-Kogalymneft (1993) into Russia's largest private oil company. He resigned as president and director in April 2022 after UK/Australian sanctions but remains its largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: In 1990, as Soviet deputy minister, he led the delegation to BP in the UK and took over the agenda, asking BP's executives to explain how a modern vertically integrated oil company should be set up - the template for Lukoil.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious coin collector: the International Numismatic Club museum, opened in 2015 in Moscow's restored 17th-century Yusupov-Zinoviev Chambers on his initiative, displays coins from his personal collection, including a Konstantin ruble and the first regular-mint gold chervonets of 1701.
notes: Sanctioned by UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand since 2022; Lukoil itself was sanctioned by the US in 2025. Very private, gives few interviews. Only company press route is Lukoil media relations, and he no longer holds a formal role there. Check sanctions/legal considerations before any outreach.

name: Linda Stephens
current_role: Co-owner/heir of Endeavor Energy Resources stake (now merged into Diamondback Energy); not involved in day-to-day operations
profile: Linda (Nagy) Stephens is the widow of Autry Stephens, the Midland, Texas wildcatter who founded Permian Basin driller Endeavor Energy Resources and died in August 2024. Endeavor was sold to Diamondback Energy for about $26B (cash plus stock), closing September 2024; her fortune derives from that family stake. Daughter Lyndal Stephens Greth chairs the family's activities.
interesting_fact: Endeavor's founder held drilling rights to ~350,000 Permian acres for decades, rebuffing offers, before the 2024 $26B sale to Diamondback.
notes: Very private; almost no public profile of her own. Reporting says she is not involved in operations. Family philanthropy runs via the Stephens Greth Family Foundation (Midland, est. 2024, led by daughter Lyndal Stephens Greth), which funded UT Austin's Autry C. Stephens Engineering Discovery Building - likely the only institutional route. No published contact found.

name: Lyndal Stephens Greth
current_role: President and director, Stephens Greth Family Foundation (Midland, TX); former chair of Endeavor Energy Resources; major Diamondback Energy shareholder
profile: Daughter of Endeavor Energy Resources founder Autry Stephens; served on Endeavor's board from 2013, became vice chairman, then chair on his death in August 2024. She oversaw the close of Endeavor's ~$26B cash-and-stock sale to Diamondback Energy (Sept 2024), leaving the Stephens family as a large FANG holder. She now leads the ~$2B Stephens Greth Family Foundation.
interesting_fact: Endeavor, built by her father from 1979, was one of the largest private U.S. oil producers (~327,000 boe/day in 2024) before the $26B Diamondback deal; she took the chair when he died months before closing.
deep_cut_fact: Her Stephens Greth Foundation gave $8M to the SPCA of Texas's 'Care Unleashed' campaign ($5M for a new building, $3M for programs), and the SPCA's Dallas campus was renamed the Stephens Greth Foundation Campus; the foundation also funded UT Austin's Autry C. Stephens Engineering Discovery Building.
notes: Very private; no public interviews or social accounts found. Foundation (EIN 99-2739395, Midland TX) has no published website/email found. Best route is likely via the foundation's registered address or Diamondback Energy's corporate office.

name: Leonid Mikhelson
current_role: Chairman of the Management Board (CEO) and co-founder, PAO Novatek; major shareholder of petrochemical group Sibur
profile: Civil engineer who built Soviet gas pipelines, privatised his pipeline-construction trust in 1991 and grew it into Novatek, Russia's largest independent gas and LNG producer (Yamal LNG, Arctic LNG 2). He also holds just over 30% of Sibur and funds the V-A-C Foundation, which turned a power station opposite the Kremlin into the GES-2 art centre (opened 2021).
interesting_fact: He spent more than $470 million converting the GES-2 power plant across from the Kremlin, designed by Renzo Piano's studio, into a contemporary art space that opened in late 2021.
deep_cut_fact: As a young man he dreamed of being a pilot (rejected for poor eyesight), then nearly left to play volleyball professionally in Tashkent before a shoulder injury ended it; in 1991 he sold his Zhiguli car to buy a 15% stake in the newly privatised pipeline company Nova.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK government in 2022 (and named on the US CAATSA 'oligarch' list in 2018); Novatek's Arctic LNG 2 is under US sanctions. Outreach from a Western podcast may be legally/politically sensitive - check sanctions rules first. Only corporate channels are public.

name: Andy Von Bechtolsheim
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Architect, Arista Networks (responsible for advanced AI, silicon and optics initiatives)
profile: German-born engineer (Andreas von Bechtolsheim) who co-founded Sun Microsystems in 1982, later Granite Systems (sold to Cisco) and Kealia, and co-founded Arista Networks, whose data-center switches power AI/cloud networks. Early angel investor in Google. Now Arista's chief architect focused on AI networking, silicon and optics (e.g. XPO liquid-cooled pluggable optics MSA, 2026).
interesting_fact: In September 1998 he wrote a $100,000 check to 'Google Inc.' before the company was even incorporated, prompting Page and Brin to formally set it up; the stake was worth at least $1B at the IPO.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he won Germany's national Jugend forscht competition in physics (1974) with an ultrasound device that precisely measured flows; at 16 he also designed an Intel 8008-based industrial controller for a local firm, programmed in binary, whose royalties helped fund his education.
notes: Press email is Arista Corporate Communications (Amanda Jaramillo) per 2026 releases. Speaks often at optics events (OFC, Optica, PIC Summit); strong fit for AI networking/optics. No personal socials found. Title moved from Chairman to Chief Architect after a 2024 SEC settlement - avoid the topic.

name: Greg Brockman
current_role: Co-founder and President, OpenAI (also leads product strategy since May 2026, plus AI infrastructure)
profile: North Dakota-raised programmer who left Harvard/MIT to join Stripe, becoming its first CTO (grew it from 4 to 250 people). Co-founded OpenAI in 2015; his stake made him a multi-billionaire. In 2026 he took charge of OpenAI's unified product team (ChatGPT, Codex, API) alongside its compute/data-center buildout.
interesting_fact: Won a silver medal at the 2006 International Chemistry Olympiad and was the first North Dakotan Intel Science Talent Search finalist since 1973.
deep_cut_fact: His first-ever paid job was an acting gig: as a scrawny ninth grader he auditioned to be a marching tin-soldier extra in a Mannheim Steamroller Christmas concert in Grand Forks. After high school he took a gap year and wrote ~100 pages of a first-principles chemistry textbook, still unfinished on his site.
notes: Publishes his own email on his homepage (obfuscated as greg [at] gregbrockman [dot] com). Very active on X as @gdb. Strong fit for AI compute/data-center topics (oversees OpenAI infrastructure). 'substack' entry is actually his personal blog.

name: Chen Tianshi
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Cambricon Technologies (SSE: 688256)
profile: Born 1985 in Nanchang, Chen entered USTC's gifted 'Special Class for the Young' as a teen and earned a CS PhD by 2010. After research at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Computing Technology, he co-founded AI-chip maker Cambricon in 2016 ('China's Nvidia'); its shares soared from 2024 on demand for domestic AI accelerators.
interesting_fact: Cambricon grew out of academic papers co-written by Chen and his elder brother Chen Yunji; both entered USTC's gifted-youth program and had CS doctorates by 24. The CAS Institute of Computing Technology still holds a minority stake.
deep_cut_fact: He was lead author of 'DianNao' (ASPLOS 2014), an early deep-learning accelerator paper reporting ~118x speedup and ~21x energy savings vs a SIMD CPU; his ICT homepage lists it as an ASPLOS'14 Best Paper Award winner, and it seeded Cambricon's chip line.
notes: No published IR/press email found on company site; investor contact is via Shanghai Stock Exchange (688256) disclosures. Media-shy; rarely gives interviews.

name: Gennady Timchenko
current_role: Founder/owner, Volga Group (private investment firm); Chairman of the Board, Kontinental Hockey League (KHL); President, SKA Saint Petersburg
profile: Russian billionaire (born 1952, Leninakan/Gyumri) who co-founded oil trader Gunvor in 1997 and built Volga Group, which holds major stakes in gas producer Novatek and petrochemical group Sibur. A close Putin associate, he is sanctioned by the US (2014) and EU/UK (2022); he sold his Gunvor stake the day before US sanctions hit.
interesting_fact: In 1998 he co-founded the Yawara-Neva judo club in Saint Petersburg (with the Rotenberg brothers; Putin is honorary president), and he has chaired the KHL hockey league since 2012.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an electrical engineer (Leningrad Mechanical Institute, 1976) and started in 1977 at the Izhorsky plant near Saint Petersburg, which built power generators; as a child he lived in East Germany (1959-65) and learned German.
notes: Sanctioned by US, EU and UK; outreach/interviews may raise legal/sanctions-compliance issues for the podcast. Contacts are for the Elena and Gennady Timchenko Foundation (Moscow), not him personally. Volga Group has no reachable public press contact found.

name: Henry Nicholas III
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Broadcom; founder of the Henry T. Nicholas, III Foundation and backer of Marsy's Law for All
profile: Electrical engineer (UCLA BS/MS/PhD) who worked at TRW and PairGain before cofounding fabless chipmaker Broadcom with Henry Samueli in 1991. He took it public in 1998 and stepped down as CEO in 2003; Broadcom's later merger with Avago drives his wealth. He now focuses on crime-victims' rights via Marsy's Law, named for his sister, and on education philanthropy.
interesting_fact: A music enthusiast, Nicholas has said his inspiration for Broadcom came from Pink Floyd lyrics; Broadcom itself was started in 1991 in a spare bedroom of his Redondo Beach home.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 he co-founded the Nicholas Academic Centers with retired Orange County Superior Court Judge Jack K. Mandel to give academic support to under-resourced Santa Ana high schoolers; he has given $57.7M and the centers have graduated 2,070 students, nearly all going on to post-secondary education.

public_contacts.value: Ted Varipatis, Serra Public Affairs - ted@serrapublicaffairs.com (press contact listed for Marsy's Law campaign)

notes: Has had widely reported legal/drug issues (2008 indictment later dismissed; 2019 Las Vegas case) - avoid. Best route is via the Marsy's Law for All organisation / its PR firm; the press contact found is on the Maine campaign page. His PhD (UCLA) was awarded in 1998.

name: Andrey Melnichenko
current_role: Founder of EuroChem (fertilizers) and SUEK (coal); left both boards in March 2022 and stepped back as beneficiary after sanctions
profile: Belarus-born Russian industrialist who started with a campus currency-exchange booth, co-founded MDM Bank at 21 (1993), then built fertilizer giant EuroChem and coal/energy company SUEK through MDM Group. Sanctioned by EU/UK/US in 2022, which he disputes; his wife became trust beneficiary of the stakes. Holds UAE citizenship since 2021.
interesting_fact: His Philippe Starck-designed Sailing Yacht A, the world's largest sail-assisted yacht, was frozen by Italian authorities in Trieste in 2022; he also collects Impressionist art including Monet.
deep_cut_fact: Studied physics at Moscow State University. At 14 he was evacuated after Chernobyl; he later called that his 'freest and most interesting summer' and wrote in The Economist (2026) it taught him 'a complex system containing enormous amounts of energy does not forgive miscalculation or arrogance.'
notes: Sanctioned by EU, UK and US (2022) - check legal/compliance before any engagement. Best route is the Andrey Melnichenko Foundation media inbox (foundation also runs the Mendeleev Chemistry Olympiad support). Has written essays for The Economist on energy/civilisation, so is open to long-form media.

name: Wang Chuanfu
current_role: Founder, Chairman and President, BYD Company Ltd.
profile: Chemist-turned-entrepreneur born 1966 in Wuwei, Anhui, who founded BYD in Shenzhen in 1995 as a rechargeable-battery maker. BYD entered autos in 2003 and is now the world's largest plug-in/EV maker, also making batteries (FinDreams/Blade), buses, energy storage and electronics; Berkshire Hathaway was an early investor (2008).
interesting_fact: Before BYD, Wang was general manager of a Shenzhen battery venture set up in 1993 by his Beijing research institute; he left in 1995 to found BYD at 29 with a CN¥250,000 loan from his cousin Lu Xiangyang.
deep_cut_fact: BYD's very first employee card, issued in 1995, belongs to Wang himself, bearing employee number 00001. He studied metallurgical physical chemistry at Central South University (grad. 1987) and earned a master's at the Beijing Non-Ferrous Metal General Research Institute (now GRINM) in 1990.
notes: SEC insider match (Lion Group Holding LGHL chairman/CEO) appears to be a different person with a similar name; ignore it. BYD IR email db@byd.com is the board-secretary/IR mailbox listed on CNInfo (Shenzhen exchange). Wang rarely gives Western interviews.

name: Jason Chang CS
current_role: Chairman, ASE Technology Holding (Taiwan; world's largest chip packaging & testing group)
profile: Jason Chang Chien-sheng (b. 1944, Shanghai; family from Wenzhou) cofounded Advanced Semiconductor Engineering (ASE) in Kaohsiung in 1984 with his brother Richard and built it into the world's largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider, now ASE Technology Holding (NYSE: ASX), a key player in advanced packaging for AI chips. He holds Singapore citizenship.
interesting_fact: Educated at National Taiwan University (BS) and the Illinois Institute of Technology (MS) before building ASE; Hurun lists him under China but he is Taiwanese-Singaporean.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2015 he received a SEMI Award recognising his 'significant achievements in the development and commercialization of copper wire in the IC assembly process' - an industry-wide switch from gold to copper bonding wire that ASE pushed early.
notes: Aged 82 and low-profile; skipped the June 2025 AGM. Hurun lists country as China but he is Taiwan-based with Singapore citizenship. Best route is ASE corporate PR/IR. corp_comms@aseglobal.com also published on the contact page.

name: Vinod Shantilal Adani
current_role: Dubai-based investor; runs a family investment office; part of the Adani Group promoter group (no formal executive title)
profile: Born 1949 in Gujarat, Vinod Adani is the elder brother of Gautam Adani. He started a textile business in Mumbai, traded commodities from Singapore from 1989 and has lived in Dubai since 1994, where he runs a family investment office. He is a Cypriot citizen, and the Adani Group lists him as a member of its promoter group.
interesting_fact: The IIFL Wealth Hurun India Rich List 2022 named him the richest NRI (non-resident Indian) and the sixth-richest Indian overall.
deep_cut_fact: He started out on his own long before Dubai. In 1976 he founded a textile business, VR Textile, in Mumbai, then moved to Singapore in 1989 to trade commodities.
notes: Very private: he keeps a low profile and has no public website or social accounts. He is central to the 2023 Hindenburg allegations and earlier DRI probes, so outreach is sensitive. If attempted at all, the realistic route is the Adani Group corporate communications office. Net-worth figures vary widely by source.

name: Dang Yanbao
current_role: Chairman, Ningxia Baofeng Energy Group (Shanghai-listed coal-to-chemicals/olefins producer); controlling holder of Baofeng Energy Storage
profile: Born 1973, Dang worked in building materials, trading and investment before founding Baofeng Energy in Ningxia in 2005, turning coal into olefins and other chemicals. In 2025 Baofeng began operating a $6.7B Inner Mongolia olefins plant, lifting capacity to 5.2M tons/yr; a sister firm began trial output at a 100GWh battery/energy-storage plant in Yinchuan in 2024.
interesting_fact: Baofeng's Inner Mongolia coal-to-olefins complex, which started up in 2025 at a cost of about $6.7 billion, is among the largest olefins plants in the world, raising company capacity to 5.2 million tons a year.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Yanchi County, Ningxia, and in 2011 he and his wife set up the Ningxia Yanbao Charity Foundation for education and poverty relief; by 2021 it had financially helped about 256,700 young students (he gave RMB 302M to it in 2019).
notes: IR email is the board-secretary/securities affairs contact listed in Baofeng Energy's 2025 interim report summary (China Securities Journal). Chinese-language outreach recommended; low international media profile.

name: Philip Anschutz
current_role: Owner, Chairman and CEO, The Anschutz Corporation (Denver); owner of Anschutz Entertainment Group (AEG)
profile: Kansas-born Denver billionaire who built fortunes in oil (from 1960s Wyoming wildcatting), railroads (Southern Pacific), telecom (Qwest), real estate and entertainment. Through AEG he owns 70+ arenas/venues, the LA Kings and a Galaxy stake; his Power Company of Wyoming is developing the Chokecherry and Sierra Madre wind project with the TransWest Express transmission line.
interesting_fact: On 320,000 acres of his Wyoming ranch land he is building one of the world's biggest wind farms (Chokecherry and Sierra Madre, ~3 GW), paired with a transmission line to carry the power to the Southwest.
deep_cut_fact: His early oil career was saved by Hollywood: when his Wyoming well near Gillette caught fire in the late 1960s, he sold Universal Studios exclusive rights to film the blaze for its John Wayne/Red Adair movie 'Hellfighters' for $100,000, which paid Adair to put it out.

public_contacts.value: mroth@aegworldwide.com (Michael Roth, AEG VP Communications, per Jan 2025 release)

name: Harold Hamm
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Continental Resources (private since 2022); founder of the Hamm Institute for American Energy at Oklahoma State University
profile: Oklahoma sharecroppers' son who turned a water-hauling trucking business into Continental Resources, pioneering horizontal drilling and fracking in North Dakota's Bakken. He took Continental private in a 2022 buyout. Now focuses on energy policy and the Hamm Institute, which in 2026 got Google.org funding for research on reliable power for AI.

current_role: Chairman (and CEO per company releases), ASE Technology Holding Co. (TWSE: 3711, NYSE: ASX)

SPIL and USI) is a key advanced-packaging/heterogeneous-integration supplier for AI chips. The brothers also invest in real estate developer Sino Horizon.

name: Edwin Chen
current_role: Founder & CEO, Surge AI

Bootstrapped with no outside funding, Surge passed $1B+ revenue in 2024 with under ~100 staff (customers include Google and Anthropic); Chen owns an estimated ~75%. Earlier he was a data/research scientist at Twitter, Google and Facebook.

name: Jayshree Ullal
current_role: Chairperson and CEO, Arista Networks; director, Snowflake
