profile: Li Min cofounded Rockchip in Fuzhou in 2001 with Huang Xu and remains chairman (reappointed general manager in Jan 2025). Rockchip designs SoCs for AIoT devices, tablets and edge-AI products and listed in Shanghai in 2020; Li holds roughly 37% of the company, the source of his fortune.
interesting_fact: Rockchip, a Fuzhou chip designer, counts Intel, Samsung and Google among its customers and focuses on intelligent IoT and edge-AI processors.
deep_cut_fact: In December 2025 he donated 175,000 Rockchip shares (worth roughly RMB 31M at the time) to the education foundation of his alma mater, Fuzhou No. 1 Middle School (福州一中), 'to give back to his alma mater'.
notes: Low media profile; English name in Chinese is 励民. Best route is via Rockchip's securities/IR department. Some unofficial sites say he was born 1965 and graduated Zhejiang University 1991 - not verified.

name: Steven Hao
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cognition (maker of the Devin AI software-engineering agent)
profile: MIT-trained competitive programmer and former early engineer at Scale AI who co-founded Cognition in late 2023 with Scott Wu and Walden Yan. Cognition's Devin autonomous coding agent (and its 2025 acquisition of Windsurf) drove rapid valuation jumps, making Hao a billionaire per Forbes.
interesting_fact: All three Cognition co-founders were International Olympiad in Informatics competitors; Forbes reported that the company's rapid growth made CTO Hao a billionaire within about two years of founding.
deep_cut_fact: At IOI 2014 in Taipei he placed 6th in the world for the United States, scoring perfect 100s on five of six problems (525/600) to win a gold medal.
notes: No published press email found; only company social accounts. CEO Scott Wu is the usual public face; Hao is the technical lead and appears at engineering conferences (e.g. GitNation speaker profile), a possible route.

name: Fan Hongwei
current_role: Chairman, Hengli Petrochemical Co. (SSE: 600346); Vice Chairman, Hengli Group
profile: Born 1967 in Wujiang, Suzhou, Fan co-founded what became Hengli Group with her husband Chen Jianhua, starting in textiles in 1994 and integrating upstream into polyester, PTA and a giant refinery-petrochemical complex on Changxing Island, Dalian. She chairs listed Hengli Petrochemical; Hengli Group posted 2024 revenue of RMB 871.5bn (Fortune Global 500 #81).
interesting_fact: Hengli's integrated 'from a drop of oil to a bolt of cloth' chain helped break foreign dominance of PX and PTA feedstocks in China; in July 2025 Fan was one of 100 private entrepreneurs given a national 'outstanding builder' award in Beijing.
deep_cut_fact: Hengli began in 1994 as the Wujiang Chemical Fiber Weaving Factory in Shengze, Suzhou, with just 27 employees; when Hengli Group was formally set up in 2003, Fan became its general manager running production and operations.
notes: hlzq@hengli.com is Hengli Petrochemical's board-office/investor mailbox (listed in 2025 and 2026 earnings-call notices); Chinese-language approach advisable. Very low international media profile.

name: Carlos
profile: Carlos Alberto Bulgheroni (1945-2016), Argentine co-owner (with brother Alejandro) of the family energy group Bridas, died on 3 September 2016. Record matched via source of wealth Bridas and shared_with Alejandro Bulgheroni.
notes: DECEASED 3 Sep 2016 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Bulgheroni). Name field is truncated ('Carlos'); country listed as Spain is wrong - he was Argentine. For Bridas/Pan American Energy, the living family principal is his brother Alejandro Bulgheroni.

name: Romesh Wadhwani
current_role: Founder & Chairman, SAIGroup (SymphonyAI, ConcertAI); Founder & Chairman, Wadhwani Foundation
profile: Romesh Wadhwani was born in Karachi in 1947. He studied at IIT Bombay and earned a PhD in electrical engineering at Carnegie Mellon. He made his fortune founding Aspect Development, then ran the software private-equity firm Symphony Technology Group. Today he heads SAIGroup, which includes the enterprise-AI companies SymphonyAI (backed by his $1B commitment) and ConcertAI. His Wadhwani Foundation funds entrepreneurship and AI-for-good work in India.
interesting_fact: Aspect Development, which he founded in 1991, was acquired by i2 Technologies in 1999 for $9.3 billion in stock. In 2020 India awarded him the Padma Shri.
deep_cut_fact: Before Aspect, he spent a decade running two startups. One was American Robot Corporation, which made computer-integrated manufacturing software. The other was Compu-Guard Corporation, an early technology-enabled energy-management company.

public_contacts.value: Chris Gale (Gale Strategies), SymphonyAI media contact: Chris@GaleStrategies.com

notes: The Compu-Guard energy-management startup is a natural hook for an energy-focused podcast. He also sits on the boards of trustees of CSIS and the Kennedy Center. The best route is SymphonyAI's PR contact.

name: Paul Foster
current_role: Founder & CEO, Franklin Mountain Investments (El Paso, TX); former founder/chairman of Western Refining
profile: A Baylor-trained CPA who kept the books for small Southwest refineries, Foster took over bankrupt El Paso Refining with partners in 1992, built Western Refining and sold it to Tesoro in 2017 ($6.4B deal). Via Franklin Mountain Investments he holds 30+ businesses (real estate, restaurants, sports); in 2025 he sold Franklin Mountain Energy for about $2.5B.
interesting_fact: He is part owner of the El Paso Chihuahuas Triple-A baseball team (via MountainStar Sports Group) and in 2007 gave $50M to help create the Paul L. Foster School of Medicine at Texas Tech in El Paso.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Lovington, New Mexico (class of 1975), he earned an accounting degree from Baylor in 1979 and then started out working at the local refinery back in Lovington before moving to El Paso.
notes: Very relevant to energy angle: serves on the Dallas Fed Energy Advisory Council and was appointed by Gov. Abbott to the ERCOT board selection committee (https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-appoints-foster-to-ercot-board-selection-committee). Best route is Franklin Mountain Investments' general inbox.

name: Torbjorn Tornqvist
current_role: Former co-founder and CEO of Gunvor Group (oil trader, since renamed Centalion); stepped down Dec 2025 in a management buyout; head of Artemis Racing sailing team
profile: Stockholm-born (1953), Geneva-based oil trader who co-founded Gunvor in 1997 and grew it into one of the world's largest independent energy traders. He bought out co-founder Gennady Timchenko's stake in 2014. In Dec 2025 he resigned as CEO and agreed to sell his ~86% stake to ~60 senior employees, partly vendor-financed; the firm has since rebranded as Centalion.
interesting_fact: He founded the Artemis Racing sailing team in 2006, which reached the Louis Vuitton Cup final in the 2013 America's Cup challenger series and helped bring Sweden back into the America's Cup.
deep_cut_fact: He came to competitive sailing late: he started crewing with Russell Coutts at the Swan Worlds, Coutts 'talked me into a TP52', and they won the MedCup and the championship in the same season, after only about three years of sailing. He still helms his own RC44 on the 44Cup circuit.
notes: No personal or office contacts published. He has left Gunvor/Centalion, so company press office is no longer a route to him. Artemis Racing (sailing) is the only active public affiliation. Avoid Russia/Timchenko/US Treasury topics; they are the context of his exit.

name: Pyotr Aven
current_role: Co-founder/shareholder of LetterOne (L1) and Alfa Group; former chairman of Alfa-Bank (2011-2022); art collector based in Surrey, UK
profile: Moscow-born economist Pyotr (Petr) Aven was Russia's minister of foreign economic relations in 1992 before joining Alfa-Bank, which he ran as president (1994-2011) and chairman until 2022. With Mikhail Fridman and partners he co-owns Alfa Group and LetterOne. Sanctioned by the EU/UK in 2022, he stepped off LetterOne's board and now focuses on his art collection and writing.
interesting_fact: He owns what is described as the largest/best private collection of Russian art (Goncharova, Petrov-Vodkin, Chagall, Kandinsky), lent to Tate, the Royal Academy, MoMA and Fondation Louis Vuitton; in 2022 he bought a building in Riga for a planned private museum.
deep_cut_fact: His collecting began in childhood with stamps and toy cars; the first painting he bought was a 1920s still life by Pavel Kuznetsov. As a young economist he was seconded to IIASA in Laxenburg, Austria, and he has lectured at Moscow's Higher School of Economics since 2007.
notes: Under EU/UK/US sanctions since 2022 - check legal/editorial implications before any engagement. petraven.info describes itself as his website (email appears in its schema.org metadata); appears to be a reputation-style site, so treat accounts linked there with some caution. Books: 'The Age of Berezovsky', 'Gaidar's Revolution' (free at petr-aven-books.com).

name: Cho Jyh-jer
current_role: Retired; former Vice Chairman of MediaTek (retired June 2015)
profile: MediaTek co-founding veteran who joined as president in 1997 when the chip designer was spun off from United Microelectronics (UMC), and was promoted to vice chairman in 2005 to focus on new products and strategy. He retired in June 2015; his wealth comes mainly from his MediaTek stake. No public role since retirement was found.
interesting_fact: One of the founding veterans who fought alongside MediaTek chairman Tsai Ming-kai from the company's optical-disc-drive chip days, before MediaTek became one of the world's top smartphone chip designers.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer from National Chiao Tung University (communication engineering), he came out of NCTU's famed 'Lab 307' under Prof. Wu Chung-yu, one of the first master's cohorts in a lab that produced many of Taiwan's IC-design leaders.
notes: Very private, retired since 2015; no published personal/office contact found. Deep-cut fact taken from search-indexed text of GVM/NYCU pages (gvm.com.tw not fetchable here) - double-check before use. Alive status not confirmed but no death report found; still on 2026 Forbes real-time list.

name: James
profile: Most likely James K. 'J.K.' Irving, chairman of J.D. Irving Ltd. and brother of Arthur Irving (Irving Oil), with whom the Hurun 2014 entry is shared. He died on 21 June 2024, aged 96, in Saint John, New Brunswick. Record skipped per instructions.
notes: Entry gives only the first name 'James' (Irving Group, shared with Arthur Irving), so identity is inferred. J.K. Irving died 21 June 2024 (https://www.cbc.ca/1.7243426); Arthur Irving died in May 2024. If the entry meant J.K.'s son James D. 'Jim' Irving (co-CEO of J.D. Irving Ltd.), he is alive and would need separate research.

name: Alejandro Bulgheroni
current_role: Chairman, Pan American Energy Group (Argentina); owner of Bulgheroni family wine estates incl. Bodega Garzón (Uruguay)
profile: Argentine industrial engineer (b. 1943, Rufino) who joined his father's Bridas Corp. in 1965 and ran it with brother Carlos from 1985; sold 50% to CNOOC and in 2017 merged with BP's Argentine assets to form Pan American Energy Group, Argentina's largest private integrated energy firm. Lives in Uruguay; owns 10+ wineries worldwide and a large dairy complex.
interesting_fact: In 1992 he secured some of the first gas exploration concessions Turkmenistan granted to a foreign energy company. His Garzón wine club membership reportedly costs $200,000.
deep_cut_fact: His wine empire began as an energy idea: in 2006 he stood on a windy Uruguayan hilltop scouting a wind-farm site, advisers suggested vines instead, and when told quality would take 6-8 years he quipped, 'How old do you think I am?' (Wine Spectator, 2018).
notes: The PAE email is the company's general 'otras consultas' inbox, not a press desk. Son Marcos Bulgheroni is PAE Group CEO. The wine/energy angle (wind farm turned vineyard) is a natural hook.

name: CC Leung
current_role: Co-founder and Vice Chairman, Quanta Computer (Taiwan)
profile: C.C. (Chee-Chun) Leung (梁次震) co-founded Quanta Computer in 1988 with fellow NTU alumnus Barry Lam, after serving as a VP at Kinpo Electronics. Quanta became the world's largest contract notebook maker and is now a leading builder of AI servers and racks for hyperscalers. He remains vice chairman and comments on the AI server outlook.
interesting_fact: A physics graduate of National Taiwan University (unlike EE-trained co-founder Barry Lam), Leung gave NT$205 million to his alma mater to support basic research.
deep_cut_fact: National Taiwan University's Leung Center for Cosmology and Particle Astrophysics (LeCosPA), founded in 2007, was created with his donation; in July 2025 it became host of the new Max Planck-IAS-NTU Center for particle physics, cosmology and geometry.
notes: Low-profile; speaks to Taiwanese press mainly at Quanta AGMs/events. No published personal or IR email found; Quanta routes media via designated spokespersons (contact via quantatw.com). LeCosPA physics connection is a strong conversation opener.

name: Lin Jianhua
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Hangzhou First Applied Material (Shanghai: 603806)
profile: Co-founded Hangzhou First Applied Material in 2003 with his wife Zhang Hong after 12 years at a state-owned fertilizer factory in Zhejiang. First became the world's largest supplier of solar-module encapsulant film (EVA/POE), with over half of the global market, plus backsheets; it has since expanded into electronic-circuit and battery materials.
interesting_fact: Before founding a solar-materials giant he spent 1982-1994 working at a state-owned fertilizer factory in Zhejiang Province.
deep_cut_fact: First did not start in solar: its early product was hot-melt adhesive web film for the textile industry, and moving into EVA solar film was what the company calls its first transformation, from textiles into new energy. It now supplies over 50% of the world's PV encapsulant film.
notes: Low public profile; rarely interviewed, company communications usually come from the board secretary (Zhang Ying). Best route is the securities/IR department email; Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Anton Osika
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Lovable (Stockholm)
profile: Swedish engineer (b. 1990) who co-founded 'vibe coding' startup Lovable with CTO Fabian Hedin in 2023 after his open-source GPT-Engineer project went viral. Lovable launched in Nov 2024, hit $100M ARR in eight months and was valued at $13.3B in Aug 2026; Forbes estimates he owns ~24%. Earlier he was first employee at Sana Labs and co-founder/CTO of Depict.ai.
interesting_fact: Lovable reached $100M in annualized subscription revenue just eight months after launch - which Forbes calls the fastest-growing software startup in history; he and Hedin pledged 50% of exit proceeds to charity via Founders Pledge.
deep_cut_fact: Before startups he was a physicist: he earned a physics BSc at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, then an MSc in engineering physics at KTH, and did research tied to the ATLAS experiment at CERN.
notes: Very accessible and media-friendly; posts constantly on X and LinkedIn and does lots of podcasts/conference talks. Best route: press@lovable.dev or a DM on X. AI-software angle more than data centers/energy.

name: Fabian Hedin
current_role: Cofounder and Chief Technology Officer, Lovable (Stockholm)
profile: Swedish engineer who, after founding small startups (Tentium, TenFAST) and leading frontend at Depict.ai, was recruited by Anton Osika to cofound Lovable out of the open-source GPT Engineer project. Lovable's 'vibe coding' platform lets non-coders build apps by prompt; it hit $100M ARR eight months after its Nov 2024 launch and was valued at $13.3B in Aug 2026. He owns ~24%.
interesting_fact: Lovable reached $100M in annualized subscription revenue just eight months after launch, which Forbes calls the fastest-growing software startup in history; Hedin and Osika have pledged 50% of exit proceeds to charity.
deep_cut_fact: His path into building software started with running his own Minecraft servers in high school, a story he told on Notion's 'First Block' founder series; Lovable also dogfoods heavily, building its own internal tools (office CRM, ops software) in Lovable.
notes: Accessible, technical founder who does podcasts/conference talks (Notion First Block, Google Cloud Next, HumanX). Best route: Lovable press@ or via conference speaker circuits. Personal X/LinkedIn not verified here (web-search budget ran out).

name: Edward Bass
current_role: President, Fine Line, Inc. (Fort Worth private investment and venture capital firm); owner/developer of Sundance Square
profile: Fort Worth-born Bass brother (Yale 1967) whose share of the Sid Richardson oil inheritance grew through oil, pipelines and investments; the brothers sold their oil company to ExxonMobil in 2017 for $5.6B in stock. Best known for remaking downtown Fort Worth via Sundance Square, Bass Performance Hall and Dickies Arena, and for funding Biosphere 2; pledged $160M to Yale's Peabody Museum.
interesting_fact: In 1991 he spent about $150 million backing Biosphere 2 in Arizona, the sealed experimental ecosystem meant to show humans could live in enclosed habitats such as those in space.
deep_cut_fact: He won the 2007 Henry Hope Reed Award (given alongside Notre Dame's Driehaus Prize) for championing traditional architecture and urbanism; as chairman of Performing Arts Fort Worth he led the building of the Bass Performance Hall, which opened in 1998.
notes: Private; no published personal/office email found. Natural routes are via Fine Line, Inc. or Sundance Square (Fort Worth). Strong interest in architecture/urbanism and ecology (Biosphere 2); emeritus Yale Corporation trustee.

name: Scott Lin
current_role: Co-founder, Largan Precision; chairman of Mao Yu Memorial Co. (Maoyu), Largan's largest single corporate shareholder (no executive role at Largan)
profile: Scott Lin (Lin Yao-ying, b. 1933) co-founded Taichung-based Largan Precision with Tony Chen in 1987; it became the world's leading smartphone-lens maker and a major Apple supplier. Largan is now run by his sons; in 2020 he moved family shares into the locked holding company Maoyu. Forbes puts his fortune at about $3B.
interesting_fact: At 93, 16 years after handing over the reins, he still goes into Largan six days a week and closely follows its push into co-packaged optics (CPO) for AI data centres, studying AI alongside staff.
deep_cut_fact: An agricultural-chemistry graduate of National Chung Hsing University, he was a middle-school chemistry teacher and worked at Taiwan Sugar and a provincial ammonium-sulfate company before moving into optics; he started Largan at about 47 with no optics background.
notes: Chinese name 林耀英. Aged 93; very low profile, Chinese-language media only. 'office_email' is Largan's general company address. Outreach likely best via Largan IR or in Mandarin; CPO/data-centre optics angle is topical.

name: John Paul DeJoria
current_role: Co-founder and chairman, John Paul Mitchell Systems; co-founder of Patron Spirits (sold to Bacardi 2018); >10% holder of HighPeak Energy
profile: Born 1944 in Echo Park, LA, DeJoria sold encyclopedias and shampoo door-to-door and was at times homeless before co-founding John Paul Mitchell Systems with Paul Mitchell in 1980 on a $700 loan. He co-founded Patron in 1989 and sold it to Bacardi in 2018 ($5.1B deal). He now invests across ventures incl. West Texas oil producer HighPeak Energy (~12% stake) and runs a family foundation.
interesting_fact: Sea Shepherd-linked Captain Paul Watson Foundation named its first anti-whaling ship the 'John Paul DeJoria II' (2022); he also bought the former McDonald's HQ campus incl. Hamburger University for $40M in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the U.S. Navy at 17 straight out of high school and served on the aircraft carrier USS Hornet; in 2012 the U.S. Navy Memorial gave him its Lone Sailor Award, and he credited the Hornet with teaching him the people-management and teamwork skills he later used in business.
notes: Very public, media-friendly speaker (Shark Tank guest, documentaries, memoir). Energy angle: HighPeak Energy 13D holder plus past interests in solar and natural gas ventures. Foundation (JP's Peace, Love & Happiness) website/Instagram are the cleanest routes; no published personal or press email found. Avoid ROKiT bankruptcies as a topic.

name: Zhu Guodong
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder (~7%) of Suzhou TFC Optical Communication (300394.SZ); no board or executive role since Nov 2023
profile: Zhu Guodong (朱国栋) is the technical co-founder of TFC Optical, set up in Suzhou in 2005 with Zou Zhinong and Ou Yang as a ceramic-ferrule maker (Zhu held 25%). TFC grew into a supplier of passive optical components and optical engines for AI data centers. Zhu was a director and VP until the 2023 board election and remains a top shareholder.
interesting_fact: TFC started with a single rice-grain-sized ceramic ferrule, a part then dominated by Japanese makers; the team produced roughly a million rejects before cracking nano-zirconia sintering and cut the price by nearly two-thirds versus imports.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, Zhu graduated from Tsinghua University in welding technology and equipment, holds Singapore permanent residency, and spent about 10 years at foreign firms, working as an engineer at Singapore's Sharikat Kian Tong Pte Ltd and Aston Air Control Pte Ltd before co-founding TFC.
notes: Very low profile; English sources almost nil. He is no longer an officer, so TFC's securities/IR office (zhengquan@tfcsz.com) is only an indirect route. Sold ~1.27% of TFC via inquiry transfer in Aug 2025. Chairman/face of TFC is Zou Zhinong.

name: Mário Araripe
current_role: Founder and majority owner, Casa dos Ventos (shares leadership with CEO Lucas Araripe)
profile: Ceará-born ITA-trained engineer who ran textile, real-estate and auto businesses (bought jeep maker Troller and sold it to Ford in 2006), then founded Casa dos Ventos in 2007, now Brazil's largest renewable developer (about a third of the country's operating wind farms). TotalEnergies owns 34% of its generation JV. The firm is now pivoting to powering data centers, incl. a large campus at Pecém.
interesting_fact: Casa dos Ventos calls data centers its main growth vector: it signed a ~US$500M renewable supply deal with Ascenty (Jan 2026) and is exclusive power supplier to a large data-center campus at the port of Pecém, Ceará, linked to ByteDance/TikTok.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Crato, Ceará, son of an engineer in Brazil's federal anti-drought works department; he trained as an aeronautical-mechanical engineer at ITA. The wind idea came from ITA classmate Odilon Camargo, who urged him to be first to map Brazil's wind potential; he then used the Troller sale cash to prospect the Northeast.
notes: Company accounts, not personal. Son Lucas Araripe is CEO and the public face for data-center strategy; Mário gives occasional interviews (Forbes Brasil, Diário do Nordeste). Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Contact form is commercially oriented; no published press email found.

name: Gao Guangrong
current_role: Chairman, Eoptolink Technology Inc. (新易盛, SZSE: 300502), Chengdu
profile: Sichuan-born (1969) optical-communications engineer who co-founded Eoptolink with five partners in 2008 and listed it on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2016. Eoptolink makes high-speed optical transceivers (400G/800G/1.6T) for AI clusters and cloud data centers and has boomed with AI build-outs, making him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Eoptolink, once focused on domestic telecom, only broke into overseas hyperscaler (e.g. Amazon) supply chains around 2019; with Innolight and TFC it is nicknamed one of China's 'Yi-Zhong-Tian' AI optical-module trio, and its market cap passed RMB 350B in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A technical-school graduate (industrial electrical automation, Chengdu Radio Machinery School), he joined the optical-communications branch of Leshan Radio Factory at 20 as a technician and stayed 10 years, then rotated through tech, purchasing, sales and management jobs before founding Eoptolink at 39.

public_contacts.value: daniel.wang@eoptolink.com (Wang Cheng, board secretary); vivi.wei@eoptolink.com (securities affairs rep)

notes: Low public profile; route via board secretary/IR. Note: CSRC issued an administrative penalty in Feb 2025 over his 2023 share sales (avoid in outreach). Strong data-center/AI angle.

name: Lisa Su
current_role: Chair, President and CEO, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)
profile: Taiwan-born, Bronx Science- and MIT-trained (BS/MS/PhD EE) semiconductor engineer who worked at Texas Instruments, IBM and Freescale before joining AMD in 2012 and becoming CEO in 2014. She led one of tech's great turnarounds; her wealth comes from AMD stock. Now she is pushing AMD's Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs into AI data centers, including a 2025 compute partnership with OpenAI, against Nvidia.
interesting_fact: At IBM she played a key role in developing the 'recipe' to replace aluminum interconnects with copper on chips without contaminating them, a technology launched in 1998 that yielded chips up to ~20% faster.
deep_cut_fact: As an MIT freshman her UROP job was 'pure grunt work' making two-inch wafers in Hank Smith's semiconductor lab in Building 39 for x-ray lithography research; that plus summer jobs at Analog Devices hooked her on semiconductors. Her PhD was among the earliest work on silicon-on-insulator (SOI).
notes: Extremely high-demand speaker; formal route is AMD Corporate Communications (corporate.pressinquiry@amd.com). Active on X (@LisaSu). Natural fit for AI data-center compute/power topics. Distant relative of Nvidia's Jensen Huang (often raised; she downplays it).

name: Cristiano Crippa
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Technoprobe S.p.A. (Euronext Milan: TPRO), since 2017
profile: Cristiano Crippa co-founded Technoprobe with his father Giuseppe Crippa (an ex-SGS/STMicroelectronics manager, d. 2025), which makes probe cards that test microchips; it is now the world's No. 2 probe-card maker with ~2,700 staff. Technoprobe listed in Milan in 2022 and later joined the FTSE MIB; Cristiano owns about 18% and has chaired the board since 2017.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Technoprobe became the first company in Italy to open a COVID vaccination hub for the general public inside its premises: a 4,300 m2 space where 160,000 doses were given to local residents over six months.
deep_cut_fact: Technoprobe started in the garage and attic of the Crippa family home in Merate (Lecco), while his father was still working at SGS/ST; in 1997 it bought its first building in nearby Cernusco Lombardone and moved in with about 10 employees. The company still lists 'Innovation makers' among its values.
notes: Founding year differs by source (Forbes: 1989 with his father; company history: garage start 1993, incorporated 1996). Family-run, low media profile; press@technoprobe.com is the published route. Father Giuseppe died July 2025 - avoid leading with that.

name: Roberto Crippa
current_role: Vice President (and Vice Chairman of the Board), Technoprobe S.p.A.
profile: Roberto Crippa is the son of the late Giuseppe Crippa (d. 2025), who founded probe-card maker Technoprobe in his garage in 1989. Roberto joined in 2002, ran Italian operations and has been Vice President since 2013; Technoprobe, whose probe cards test chips before packaging (including for AI processors), listed on Euronext Milan in 2022 and Roberto owns about 18%.
interesting_fact: Technoprobe began in 1989 in Giuseppe Crippa's garage and attic while he was still working at STMicroelectronics; it became a global top probe-card supplier and made the founder a billionaire in his late 80s.
deep_cut_fact: A chemical engineer from Politecnico di Milano, he started in a technical product-development role and is author or co-author of numerous international patents; in 2018 he and brother Cristiano led the 100% acquisition of hydraulics-components engineer DA-TOR, starting a diversification into an Italian industrial hub.
notes: Forbes named him among Italy's top 100 managers in 2019. Gave a 2023 interview to Corriere della Sera's L'Economia (https://technoprobe.com/news-and-press/news-events-publications/leconomia-interview-with-roberto-crippa). Company is in Cernusco Lombardone (Lecco). info@ is a general company address.

name: Michael S. Smith
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Freeport LNG (Houston); director, Teledyne Technologies
profile: Made his first fortune with Basin Exploration, an E&P company he founded in Fort Collins in 1981 and sold to Stone Energy in 2001 for ~$428M. He founded Freeport LNG in 2002 as an import terminal, then flipped it to exports when shale arrived, raising $15B+ of debt to build three liquefaction trains in Freeport, Texas (~15 Mtpa). He still runs it and speaks publicly on U.S. LNG export economics.
interesting_fact: Freeport LNG was designed to import gas; when the shale boom hit he turned the strategy 180 degrees and built one of the largest U.S. LNG export terminals instead.
deep_cut_fact: Though he left CSU just shy of a chemistry degree, his 2016 $13M gift to Colorado State created 50 full-tuition business scholarships for the college's 50th anniversary and completed funding for the Michael Smith Natural Resources Building; he credited 'strong science and mathematics' at CSU for teaching him the oil business.
notes: Company is private. Freeport LNG press releases list media contact Heather Browne, Director Corporate Communications (phone 713-980-2888, office line), e.g. https://freeportlng.com/files/docs/FINAL-Restart-Press-Release-022123-2.pdf. Info@ email dates from a 2018 release. Speaks at CERAWeek/Milken - conference route possible.

name: Ravi Ruia
current_role: Co-founder and Vice Chairman, Essar Group (senior family figure since brother Shashi's death in Nov 2024)
profile: Co-founded Essar with elder brother Shashi in 1969, growing it from a Chennai port construction contract into a conglomerate spanning steel, oil refining, power, ports and telecom. Essar bought the Stanlow refinery (Essar Oil UK, now EET Fuels) from Shell in 2011 and sold its Indian refiner to a Rosneft-led group for $12.9bn in 2017; it now pursues energy-transition projects at Stanlow.
interesting_fact: The name Essar comes from the brothers' initials, 'S' and 'R' (Shashi and Ravi); the group's first job was a 1969 contract worth about Rs 2.3 crore to build an outer breakwater for Chennai (Madras) Port.
deep_cut_fact: He is a mechanical engineer by training, a graduate of the College of Engineering, Guindy in Chennai - India's oldest engineering college (founded 1794) - and was singled out as one of its six most notable alumni when it turned 225 in 2018.
notes: Essar's corporate press contacts are on essar.com press releases (Essar Capital corporate affairs) and EET Fuels (Stanlow) releases, but those sites blocked automated fetching, so no email was verified. Forbes profile is joint with Shashi Ruia (died 2024). Best route: Essar corporate affairs office.

name: Walter Faria
current_role: Owner and controlling shareholder, Grupo Petrópolis (Itaipava, Crystal, Petra, Black Princess beers), Brazil
profile: Brazilian brewer (b. 1955, Pedranópolis, SP) who went from a cotton gin to Brazil's largest Schincariol distributor, then bought Cervejaria Petrópolis in 1998 at ~2% market share; by 2013 Itaipava made it Brazil's No. 2 brewer. The group also makes TNT energy drink - likely the source of the 'energy' tag, not the energy sector.
interesting_fact: Under Faria, Grupo Petrópolis grew from about 2% of Brazil's beer sales in 1998 to over 11% and the No. 2 national brand in 2013, largely through aggressive marketing and low prices.
deep_cut_fact: At 13, in the Macedônia district of Fernandópolis (SP), he sold eggs and piglets around town using a horse cart - a cart he kept as a keepsake. His savings then funded a coffee-processing business with a brother.

public_contacts.value: VCRP Brasil (press relations for Grupo Petrópolis, South/Southeast, appointed 2024)

notes: Very private, gives no interviews. Carries significant legal baggage (Lava Jato 2019 arrest; group filed for judicial recovery in 2023) - poor fit and sensitive; avoid these topics. Weak link to the energy theme (beverages only). Company site blocks automated access; press route is via the group's PR agencies.

name: Garibaldi Thohir
current_role: Vice President Commissioner, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (formerly Adaro Energy; stepped down as President Director at the June 2025 AGM)
profile: Garibaldi 'Boy' Thohir, son of Astra co-founder Teddy Thohir and brother of Erick Thohir, led the 2005 takeover of coal miner Adaro and ran it for ~2 decades, steering it toward aluminium smelting, minerals and renewables (now AlamTri; coal spun off as AADI in 2024). He is also a tech investor (ex-Gojek commissioner).
interesting_fact: He served as president commissioner of Gojek after founder Nadiem Makarim joined the cabinet in 2019, and has said he advised Nadiem informally for years before Gojek scaled.
deep_cut_fact: Back from his US MBA, he wanted a $2,000-a-month job at Citibank, but his father refused and told him to be an entrepreneur. His first venture (1991) was a plan to build a rental office on a 3,000 m2 plot along the new Saharjo-Kuningan road in Jakarta; it stalled because land clearances required at least 1 hectare.
notes: Widely known as 'Boy Thohir'. corsec@ is AlamTri's corporate secretary (company office, not personal). Some data sites still list him as President Director - outdated since June 2025. Energy-transition angle: AlamTri is building an aluminium smelter and hydro/renewables in North Kalimantan.

name: Semahat Arsel
current_role: Chair, Vehbi Koç Foundation board & executive committee; board member, Koç Holding; chair, Divan Group
profile: Semahat Sevim Arsel (b. 1928, Ankara) is the eldest child of Koç Group founder Vehbi Koç and holds a stake in Koç Holding, Turkey's largest conglomerate (energy via Tüpraş, Aygaz, autos, appliances, banking). On Koç's board since 1964, she built its tourism/hospitality arm and leads the family's main foundation.
interesting_fact: Turkey's only postgraduate nursing education center, SANERC (founded 1992 at the American Hospital, Istanbul), is named after her; she has chaired the Vehbi Koç Foundation's Nursing Committee since its nursing fund began in 1974.
deep_cut_fact: In 1972 she took charge of renovating Istanbul's Divan Hotel in Elmadağ and went on to turn 'Divan' into a luxury hospitality brand; she also co-founded TUGEV, a foundation for tourism training, and lived in Germany in 1959-60, studying at the Goethe Institute.
notes: Aged 98 and very private; no personal public channels. Best route is via the Vehbi Koç Foundation or Koç Holding corporate communications. Koç's energy link (Tüpraş refining, Aygaz, Entek power) is the podcast angle.

name: Lukas Henrik Lundin
profile: Swedish-Canadian resource financier who chaired the Lundin Group of mining and energy companies for 25+ years (Lundin Mining, Lucara Diamond, Filo Mining, NGEx etc.); family holdings were held via the Nemesia trust vehicle. He died on 26 July 2022 in Geneva, aged 64, after a two-year battle with brain cancer.
notes: Deceased 26 July 2022 (sources: https://www.mining.com/?p=1096241 ; https://filomining.mediaroom.com/2022-07-27-Filo-Minings-Founder-and-Former-Chairman-Lukas-H-Lundin-Passes-Away). Sons Adam and Jack Lundin now lead Lundin Group companies; the Lundin family remains long-term shareholders.

name: Guo Jianjun
current_role: Listed by Hurun under 'Huineng' (likely Inner Mongolia Huineng Group, Ordos coal/coal-to-gas); role not verified
profile: Hurun lists Guo Jianjun (郭建军) with wealth from 'Huineng', an energy business. The best-known match, Inner Mongolia Huineng Group (Ordos; coal, coal chemicals, coal-to-gas, new energy), is publicly led by chairman Guo Jinshu (郭金树); no public source found linking Guo Jianjun to the group.
notes: Identity unresolved: searches find Huineng Group chairman Guo Jinshu, not Guo Jianjun; possibly a relative, another executive, or a Hurun name variant. Do not conflate with Maj. Gen. Guo Jianjun (PLA, Ningxia). Verify via Hurun's Chinese list or company registry before outreach.

name: Hilmi Panigoro
current_role: President Director, PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MedcoEnergi), Jakarta
profile: Bandung-born geologist and younger brother of Medco founder Arifin Panigoro. Joined Medco as a director in 1998 and has run or overseen it since (President Director 2001-08 and again from 2015). MedcoEnergi spans oil & gas across Southeast Asia, power (incl. geothermal/solar) and a stake in copper-gold miner Amman Mineral.
interesting_fact: Holds an ITB geological engineering degree (1981), Thunderbird MBA core program (1984) and an MSc from the Colorado School of Mines (1988); he has over four decades in oil and gas and leads a company that has set net-zero targets.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1981 as a wellsite geologist at Huffco/Vico Indonesia, rising to VP & Director of Business Process Reengineering before his brother invited him to join Medco as a director in 1998.
notes: Regular speaker at energy conferences (SPE, Singapore International Energy Week) and has given interviews on energy transition, so reachable via MedcoEnergi corporate communications/IR.

name: Ilya Sutskever
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI), Palo Alto / Tel Aviv
profile: Soviet-born Israeli-Canadian AI scientist (b. 1986) who co-created AlexNet with Hinton and Krizhevsky, co-founded OpenAI and served as chief scientist through GPT/ChatGPT and o1-style reasoning. He left in 2024 to co-found SSI, which raised $3B+ at a ~$32B valuation; CEO since July 2025. In July 2026 SSI announced an NVIDIA partnership to scale its compute 10x.
interesting_fact: He won the NeurIPS Test of Time Award three years in a row (2022-2024) and received the National Academy of Sciences Award for the Industrial Application of Science in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Jerusalem he began taking Open University of Israel classes in eighth grade; after moving to Canada at 16 he spent only about a month in high school before the University of Toronto admitted him straight into third year.
notes: Very media-shy; rare interviews (e.g. Dwarkesh Podcast, Nov 2025). SSI is compute-heavy (NVIDIA deal, earlier Google Cloud TPUs) - relevant data-center angle. comms@ssi.inc is the only published inquiry address.

name: Andre Desmarais
current_role: Deputy Chairman, Power Corporation of Canada and Power Financial Corporation
profile: André Desmarais, born in Ottawa in 1956, is the youngest son of Paul Desmarais Sr., who took control of Power Corporation in 1968. He and his brother Paul Jr. ran the Montreal holding company as co-CEOs for about 24 years, until 2020. He remains deputy chairman and sits on group boards including Great-West Lifeco, IGM Financial and Power Sustainable, its renewable-energy and sustainable-investing arm.
interesting_fact: He is honorary chairman of the Canada China Business Council and served on the Hong Kong Chief Executive's Council of International Advisers from 1998 to 2007.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career at Campeau Corporation in 1979 and was a special assistant to Canada's Minister of Justice in 1980-81 before joining Power Corp in 1983. He also started and owned an experimental farm in Canada.

public_contacts.value: Media requests: Stéphane Lemay, VP, General Counsel & Secretary, Power Corporation of Canada (phone listed on contact page; no email published)

notes: No personal social accounts were found. The best route is Power Corporation's media-requests contact. For the energy angle, Power Sustainable (renewables and energy infrastructure) is the relevant group company. The first contact entry is a named media contact with a published phone number only; no email is published.

name: Paul Desmarais Jr.
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Power Corporation of Canada (and Power Financial); also long-time chairman of Groupe Bruxelles Lambert
profile: Eldest son of Power Corp builder Paul Desmarais Sr. (born Sudbury, 1954; McGill BComm, INSEAD MBA). He joined Power Corp in 1981, led the creation of Power Financial in 1984 and was co-CEO of Power Corp from 1996 until stepping back in 2020; he remains chairman. Power's holdings span Great-West Lifeco, IGM Financial, GBL, Sagard and Power Sustainable.
interesting_fact: He sat on the boards of major European energy groups, serving as a director of GDF Suez (2008-2014) and of Total until 2017, via the family's stakes held through Pargesa/Groupe Bruxelles Lambert.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm in 1981 he cut his teeth at S.G. Warburg & Co. in London and at Standard Brands in New York; in 1984 he led the creation of Power Financial Corporation.
notes: Hurun lists 'Energy' but wealth is Power Corp (financial holding co.); energy angle is Power Sustainable (renewables/infrastructure, media contact pr@powersustainable.com per https://powersustainable.com/en/news/power-sustainable-announces-plan-to-invest-and-mobilize-more-than-10-billion-into-canadian-infrastructure-and-related-companies/). Power Corp 2026 releases list Stephane Lemay (VP, General Counsel & Secretary, 514-286-7400) as contact. Do not confuse with son Paul Desmarais III (Sagard CEO).

name: Surender Pal Singh Saluja
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Premier Energies Ltd (Hyderabad solar cell & module maker; listed NSE/BSE 2024)
profile: Mechanical engineer who founded Premier Energies in Hyderabad in 1995, starting with solar lanterns and streetlights. The company grew into one of India's largest integrated solar cell and module manufacturers and listed in Sept 2024, making him a billionaire. His son Chiranjeev Singh Saluja is MD; the firm is expanding cell, module and storage capacity.
interesting_fact: Premier Energies began in 1995 selling small solar products such as lanterns and streetlights, decades before India's solar-manufacturing boom; it is now among the country's largest makers of solar cells and modules.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated in mechanical engineering from Karnatak University, Dharwad, in 1969 and ran small ventures before solar; he has said his one slight regret is never having worked as an employee at a corporation early in his career.

public_contacts.value: mohit.chawla@premierenergies.com (Mohit Chawla, Marketing & Communications, Premier Energies)

notes: Name also spelled Surendar Singh Saluja. Day-to-day public face of the company is son and MD Chiranjeev Saluja; route through company communications. Strong energy/solar-manufacturing fit.

name: Lee Bass
current_role: Private investor (Lee M. Bass, Inc., Fort Worth); rancher and conservationist; Chairman Emeritus, The Peregrine Fund
profile: Lee M. Bass is one of the four Fort Worth Bass brothers who turned an inheritance from oilman uncle Sid Richardson into multibillion-dollar fortunes through oil and investing; in 2017 the brothers sold their oil company to ExxonMobil for $5.6B in stock. He runs his own investments, raises longhorns on South Texas ranches and is a leading Texas conservation philanthropist.
interesting_fact: He chaired the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission (named chair by Gov. George W. Bush; chairman emeritus since 2001) and with wife Ramona funded the reintroduction of the endangered Aplomado falcon in South Texas; they entered the Texas Conservation Hall of Fame in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: He is a founding member of the International Rhino Foundation, and he and Ramona helped found 'South Texas Natives' (now the Texas Native Seeds Program) at the Caesar Kleberg Wildlife Research Institute; he has also chaired the TPWD White-Tailed Deer Advisory Committee.
notes: Very private; no personal website or social accounts found. Plausible indirect routes: The Peregrine Fund (peregrinefund.org) or Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation, where he holds honorary/emeritus roles - neither publishes a contact for him personally.

name: Guillermo Rauch
current_role: Founder and CEO, Vercel
profile: Self-taught engineer from Lanús, Argentina, who never finished high school; joined the MooTools core team as a teen and moved to San Francisco at 18. Created Socket.IO and Mongoose, sold Cloudup to Automattic, then founded ZEIT (2015), now Vercel, maker of Next.js and the v0 AI app builder; valued at $9B in Sept 2025.
interesting_fact: His Socket.IO library's underlying engine powers Notion's real-time sync and powered Coinbase's first trading product; he also wrote one of the first books on Node.js, 'Smashing Node.js: JavaScript Everywhere'.
deep_cut_fact: He credits a now-defunct online hacking wargame, Izhal.com (level 1 was solved by finding a hidden HTML comment; later levels meant disassembling binaries and writing keygens), with teaching him reverse engineering and debugging more than any coding tutorial did.
notes: Very public and podcast-friendly; extremely active on X (@rauchg), which is the most direct route. Frequent guest on dev/startup podcasts.

name: Johnny Ho
current_role: Cofounder and Chief Strategy Officer, Perplexity
profile: Former competitive programmer and Harvard math/CS student who worked as a Quora engineer and a quant trader at Tower Research before cofounding Perplexity in August 2022 with Aravind Srinivas, Denis Yarats and Andy Konwinski. The AI answer engine, which cites its sources, hit a $20B valuation in 2025; Ho focuses on product strategy.
interesting_fact: Perplexity is backed by Jeff Bezos, Yann LeCun and Google chief scientist Jeff Dean, and blends multiple AI models to give footnote-style cited answers.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2012 International Olympiad in Informatics in Italy he ranked first in the world with a perfect 600/600 score for the USA team; he also won gold in 2011 and silver in 2013.
notes: Input lists an AvePoint (AVPT) directorship: that belongs to a different person, John Ho of Janchor Partners, not the Perplexity cofounder. Forbes calls him a three-time IOI gold medalist; official IOI stats show gold 2011, gold (1st) 2012, silver 2013. No verified personal social/press email found; route via Perplexity communications.

name: Zhao Lidong
current_role: Co-founder, chairman and board secretary, Enflame Technology (燧原科技, STAR Market 688801), Shanghai
profile: Tsinghua graduate who spent 20+ years in Silicon Valley semiconductors (senior director of product engineering at AMD), returned in 2014 as a VP at Tsinghua Unigroup, then co-founded Tencent-backed cloud AI-chip maker Enflame with ex-AMD colleague Zhang Yalin in 2018. Enflame listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on Sept 11, 2026 (~CNY 6.1B raise); he directly holds ~9%.
interesting_fact: Enflame started in a temporary office of under 100 sq m in Shanghai's Zhangjiang; eight years later its STAR Market IPO was 6,109x oversubscribed online and closed day one at a CNY 170.85B market value.
deep_cut_fact: He says 'product definition is the soul of a chip' and deliberately chose not to make Enflame CUDA-compatible, arguing that would doom it to be a follower; instead it built a DSA architecture and its own full software stack, TopsRider, from scratch.
notes: Forbes lists him under the US (likely US citizenship from Silicon Valley years). No personal social media found; Enflame's site blocked automated access, so no IR/press email verified - check the board office contact in the SSE listing announcement. Strong data-center/AI-chip fit; interviews are mainly in Chinese.

name: Xu Jiankang
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Powerlong Group (Powerlong Real Estate Holdings, HKEX: 1238); also known as Hoi Kin Hong
profile: Xu Jiankang (许健康, Hoi Kin Hong), born 1952 in Jinjiang, Fujian, moved to Macau and started his first company in 1981, then founded Powerlong in 1990 to develop property in Fujian; it grew into a Shanghai-based developer and mall operator. He has served on China's national CPPCC as a Macau representative.
interesting_fact: He served four consecutive terms (10th-13th) on the national CPPCC, seated as a specially invited Macau representative.
deep_cut_fact: He comes from Anhai town in Jinjiang, Fujian, and started out in business in Macau, founding his first company there in 1981, nine years before Powerlong.
notes: Alive status not freshly confirmed (no recent source checked; web-search budget exhausted). Powerlong is a property developer, weak fit for energy/data-center themes; the group went through offshore debt restructuring. Powerlong's site did not render from here, so no published IR email captured. Not data-center/energy relevant.

name: Zhang Yuqiang
current_role: Chairman of the board, Zhenshi Holding Group; vice chairman, China Jushi (stepped down as Jushi general manager in March 2024)
profile: Zhang Yuqiang built a small township cloth mill in Tongxiang, Zhejiang into China Jushi, the world's largest fiberglass maker (now part-owned by state-backed China National Building Material). His Zhenshi Holding Group also spans special steel and composites; its unit Zhejiang Zhenshi New Materials (wind-blade fiberglass fabrics) listed in Shanghai on 29 Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: In the 1980s his Tongxiang factory still drew glass fibre from clay crucibles; a 1995 visit to PPG's automated US lines spurred the push to tank-furnace technology that made Jushi the global leader.
deep_cut_fact: In 1971, aged 16, he started as a water carrier at the Dongfeng cloth mill in Shimen town, Tongxiang, hauling two to three hundred buckets a day; that mill later became the Tongxiang fiberglass factory that grew into Jushi.
notes: Chinese name 张毓强. Chinese-language media only; no personal public channels found. info@jushi.com is China Jushi's general/investor-page address. Zhenshi New Materials (601112.SH) is chaired by a family member; Zhenshi Holding site not reachable in this pass.

name: Huang Xu
current_role: Co-founder and second-largest shareholder (~14.8%) of Rockchip Electronics (603893.SH, Fuzhou); long-time director (may have left the board at the Jan 2025 re-election)
profile: Huang Xu (黄旭) co-founded Fuzhou Rockchip Electronics in 2001 with chairman Li Shi (励民). Rockchip designs SoCs for tablets, set-top boxes, AIoT and edge-AI devices (RK3588 etc.) and listed in Shanghai in 2020. As of mid-2025 he held 62.43M shares (14.84%), second only to Li Shi.
interesting_fact: Rockchip started in Nov 2001 with just RMB 1M registered capital from four founders; Huang Xu later sold part of his stake to Li Shi in 2013-14, making Li the controlling shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: Per Rockchip's listing history, Huang Xu was the largest founding investor: on 8 Nov 2001 he put in RMB 430,000 of the RMB 1M registered capital, vs RMB 400,000 from Li Shi and smaller sums from Nie Zhigan and Wu Weitun.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or bio found. Current board list (10jqka) shows Li Shi, Wang Haimin, Liu Yue, Chen Hui, so verify whether Huang still holds a board seat. Best route is Rockchip's securities/IR office (ir@rock-chips.com, Fuzhou). Listed as a natural-person shareholder in the H1 2025 report.

name: Monica Crippa
current_role: Shareholder (~12%) in Technoprobe S.p.A. (Euronext Milan: TPRO); no executive or board role (left the board in 2022)
profile: Daughter of Giuseppe Crippa (d. 2025), who started Technoprobe in 1989 in his garage and attic while still at STMicroelectronics. The Lecco-area company makes probe cards that test chips, earns ~97% of revenue abroad and listed on Euronext Milan in 2022. Monica left the board in 2022 and owns about 12%; her brothers run the business.
interesting_fact: Technoprobe began in Giuseppe Crippa's home, refining chip-testing probe cards in his kitchen/garage after hours from his ST job; it is now one of the world's top probe-card makers, supplying the biggest chipmakers.
deep_cut_fact: Unlike her engineer brothers, Monica was described in a local profile of the family business as a teacher ('insegnante') while also being part of the company alongside her mother Maria Rosa.
notes: Very private; no public profile, interviews or social accounts found. Only routes are via Technoprobe IR/communications (press contact is the company's Communication & Marketing Manager). Family holding is T-Plus. Brothers Cristiano/Roberto Crippa are the public faces.

name: Zheng Guangwen (郑广文)
current_role: Chairman, general manager and actual controller, Shenyang Fortune Precision Equipment Co. (富创精密, SSE STAR: 688409)
profile: Shenyang-based entrepreneur who controls Fortune Precision, China's leading maker of precision parts for semiconductor equipment (process/structural parts, modules, gas lines) supplying NAURA, AMEC and global tool makers. Founded 2008 and listed on the STAR Market in 2022; its 2024 revenue was RMB 3.04bn and it bought Germany's Compart Systems to broaden its platform.
interesting_fact: Fortune Precision is one of the few Chinese firms in the supply chains of top global chip-equipment makers; its shares rose roughly 450% in a year to 2026, lifting Zheng's stake to roughly RMB 7.9bn.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in the car-trading business and crossed into industrial manufacturing in 2003 by investing in Shenyang Advanced (沈阳先进), an affiliate of the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Shenyang Institute of Automation, before co-founding Fortune Precision in June 2008.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts found. Route via company securities dept (board secretary Liang Qianqian, tel 024-31692129 per filings). Caution: in Dec 2025 part of his holding company stake was frozen in connection with an investigation he was assisting (company said unrelated to operations). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Dan Wilks
current_role: Co-founder/co-owner, Wilks Brothers LLC (Cisco, Texas); founder and principal stockholder of ProFrac / PF Holdings (ACDC) via THRC Holdings
profile: Texas mason-turned-fracking billionaire. With brother Farris he founded Wilks Masonry (1995) and frac company Frac Tech (2002), selling their 70% stake in 2011 for $3.5B. Via Wilks Brothers they now control oilfield-services firm ProFrac (run by his son Matt), invest in oil, gas and data firms, and own 670,000+ acres across the West.
interesting_fact: The Wilks brothers are among America's largest private landowners (~672,000 acres in six western states) and reportedly spend about four months a year in Montana building homes on their ranches.

public_contacts.value: https://ir.pfholdingscorp.com/ (IR contact form incl. Press/Media option)
https://www.wilksbrothers.com/ (family office site; no contact listed)

notes: Very private; lives in Cisco, TX. Prominent conservative political/media donor (Daily Wire, PragerU) - sensitive context. ProFrac is now led by his son Matt Wilks (Exec Chairman, CEO from Aug 2026); best route is via ProFrac/PF Holdings IR.

name: Feridun Gecgel
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (~80%), Astor Enerji A.S. (Borsa Istanbul: ASTOR); board member, Fenerbahce Futbol A.S.
profile: Born in Sanliurfa in 1970, Gecgel became an entrepreneur straight after high school, selling electrical materials through Ozguney Elektrik and making furniture, then bought transformer maker Astor in 2005 for about $3M. Astor is now Turkey's largest maker of transformers and switchgear, exporting to 90+ countries; its 2023 Istanbul IPO made him a billionaire, and it is expanding into US grid-equipment supply.
interesting_fact: He bought Astor for roughly $3 million in 2005; after its 2023 IPO the company's market value rose to about $4 billion (pre-IPO value ~$750M).
deep_cut_fact: A football executive as well as an industrialist: in 2026 he joined Aziz Yildirim's Fenerbahce leadership, and was named to the Fenerbahce Futbol A.S. board at its 23 July 2026 extraordinary general assembly (earlier he served on MKE Ankaragucu's board).
notes: Heads-up: on 26 Sep 2026 Istanbul prosecutors placed precautionary measures on his personal cash/securities in a fund investigation (the measure on Astor itself was lifted next day); he publicly said he was on a planned US business trip. Do due diligence before outreach. Contacts are company-level only; good grid/transformer-shortage angle.

name: Liang Qin
current_role: Chairwoman and legal representative, Yangzhou Yangjie Electronic Technology (300373.SZ)
profile: Liang Qin (梁勤) has run Yangjie since 2000, first as GM of Yangzhou Yangjie Electronics and as chair since 2006. Yangjie is a vertically integrated (IDM) power-semiconductor maker - diodes, MOSFETs, IGBT modules and SiC devices for autos, AI, clean energy and 5G - listed in Shenzhen in 2014, with about 7,900 staff. She also serves on the executive committee of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce.
interesting_fact: Yangjie's business scope extends beyond chips into distributed solar: it is licensed to develop and build PV power projects and sell solar modules alongside its power semiconductors.
deep_cut_fact: She studied electronic instruments at Yangzhou Technician College (1986-89), then worked in the trade-union office of the Yangzhou Grand Hotel (1989-93) before earning an electrical-technology degree at Yangzhou University; she has been named a Jiangsu Province Model Worker.
notes: Contacts are company-level (board secretary's office, secretary Qin Nan). Active in Jiangsu business-federation and women-entrepreneur bodies; Chinese-language outreach advisable. Power semis/SiC angle fits energy and data-center topics.

name: Wu Yingming
current_role: Executive Director and President of Regional Management, CATL (Contemporary Amperex Technology); chairman of CATL's board of supervisors 2015-Dec 2025
profile: Wu Yingming (b. 1967) is a longtime CATL executive and shareholder whose fortune comes from his stake in the Ningde-based lithium-ion battery giant. He joined CATL in Dec 2015 as procurement & IT director, chaired its board of supervisors for a decade, and in Dec 2025 became an executive director overseeing subsidiary management and zero-carbon ecosystem business; he also runs several CATL JVs, e.g. CATL-SAIC Power Battery.
interesting_fact: Before CATL he was procurement and IT director (2006-2012) at Dongguan Amperex Technology (ATL), the consumer-battery maker from which CATL was spun off in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: He is a software engineer by training: he earned a bachelor's in computer software from Northeast Institute of Technology (now Northeastern University) in July 1989, and his first CATL post combined procurement with IT. He is also general manager of CATL's JV with SAIC (Shidai SAIC Power Battery).
notes: Low public profile; route via CATL IR/press. Board change: nominated non-independent director 6 Dec 2025 when the supervisory board was restructured (https://tech.ifeng.com/c/8orI8gQ7OKQ). Forbes profile still lists him as supervisory-board chairman.

name: Teo Swee Ann
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Espressif Systems (Shanghai STAR Market: 688018)
profile: Singaporean EE (NUS master's, 2000) who worked at Bluetooth startup Transilica, then Marvell and Montage Technology, before founding Espressif in Shanghai in 2008. Espressif's low-cost ESP8266/ESP32 Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chips power vast numbers of IoT devices; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2019 and he still runs it.
interesting_fact: Espressif's ESP8266, a cheap Wi-Fi microcontroller, has been described as 'legendary' in the maker world; he started the company wanting to automate analogue chip design and at one point ran it as a design consultancy before making his own chips.
deep_cut_fact: His maths teacher at The Chinese High School, Mr Chew Kim Liong, entered him untrained into a national maths competition where he placed seventh, earning advanced number-theory classes; Teo says Chew 'changed the trajectory of my life'. He also chose to minor in law at NUS despite expecting to do poorly in it.
notes: Engineer-founder who answers press by email/chat (per Schoolbag). Publishes 'CEO Messages' on Espressif's site. No dedicated press email found; IR email is the only Espressif-published address. Forbes bio empty in input.

name: Ron Corio
current_role: Founder and former CEO of Array Technologies (Nasdaq: ARRY); private investor in Albuquerque, New Mexico
profile: Founded solar-tracker maker Array Technologies in Albuquerque in 1989, moving from home trackers to the horizontal single-axis trackers now standard on utility-scale solar farms after a first 250 kW BP Solar project in 2001. He stepped down as CEO in 2018, sold his ~38% stake for about $1.2bn within six months of the Oct 2020 IPO, and left the board in 2022.
interesting_fact: Forbes calls him the 'Godfather of Solar' and New Mexico's first (and only) billionaire; he now prefers to stay out of the spotlight.
deep_cut_fact: In Array's early days he built a solar tracker that hung from Steve Fossett's balloon on his first round-the-world attempt (keeping a flexible PV array pointed at the sun as the balloon rotated), supplied 'artistic trackers' for Robin Williams' Napa Valley home, and made fold-out tracking power trailers for anti-poaching patrols in Africa.
notes: Very private; no personal site, social accounts or office contact found. Array Technologies IR/press would not represent him since he left the board in 2022. Home Power magazine praised his first home tracker in a 1991 'Things That Work' review - good rapport hook for an energy podcast.

name: Huang Jianjun
current_role: Director and General Manager, Suzhou Semight Instruments (联讯仪器, SSE STAR: 688808); one of its three joint actual controllers
profile: Huang Jianjun (黄建军, b. 1981) is GM of Semight Instruments, a Suzhou maker of optical-communication and semiconductor test equipment for 400G/800G/1.6T optical modules used in AI data centers. Gotion makes LFP/NMC cells and cathode/anode materials, listed in Shenzhen in 2015, raised $685M on SIX Swiss in 2022, and counts Volkswagen as a ~24% shareholder.

name: Igor Yusufov
current_role: Former Russian Minister of Energy (2001-04) and founder of Fund Energy; per Forbes Russia, no longer manages projects (since 2020) and divested declared assets by March 2022
profile: Dagestan-born (1956) power engineer turned official: ran the state reserves agency, served as Russia's energy minister 2001-04, then presidential envoy for international energy cooperation and a Gazprom board member (2003-13). After 2011 he invested via Fund Energy in oil and gas, mining and renewables, but Forbes Russia reports he exited those holdings by 2022.
interesting_fact: As energy minister he initiated the first Russian-American Business Energy Summit in Houston (Oct 2002), co-signing a joint statement with U.S. Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham and Commerce Secretary Donald Evans.
deep_cut_fact: Before government he was a working power engineer: after Novocherkassk Polytechnic he worked at Mosenergo, then spent four years in Cuba as a technology expert on the construction site of a Havana thermal power plant.
notes: Dropped off Forbes lists (listed as 'former'); says he has exited his assets. No published contact found; former company site corporationenergy.ru may be stale. Outreach to a former Russian minister may raise sanctions/compliance questions; check before contacting. Low fit unless covering Russian energy history.

name: Sanjay Mehrotra
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Micron Technology (MU); director, CDW
profile: Kanpur-born (1958) electrical engineer (UC Berkeley BS/MS) who co-founded SanDisk in 1988 with Eli Harari and Jack Yuan and was its CEO 2011-2016 until the Western Digital sale. CEO of Micron since 2017, he has steered it into the AI boom via high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for data-center GPUs, which drove Micron's surge and his billionaire status.
interesting_fact: He holds dozens of flash-memory patents and was elected to the US National Academy of Engineering in 2022 for contributions to multilevel-cell (MLC) NAND flash design that made dense flash storage practical.
deep_cut_fact: Supporting himself from 18, his first job at Berkeley was collecting dirty dishes in the International House dining room - he quit after a few days to grade homework. Later, in 1984, he was slated to be one of four Atmel co-founders with mentor George Perlegos, but stayed at Seeq out of loyalty.
notes: Public-company CEO; requests go via Micron corporate communications. Very strong data-center/AI memory angle (HBM). Gave a 2019 Computer History Museum oral history, useful for prep.

name: Zhang Jianhui
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, HyperStrong (Beijing HyperStrong Technology / 海博思创, Shanghai STAR Market)
profile: Dr. Zhang Jianhui (张剑辉) founded HyperStrong in Beijing in 2011 after studying at Tsinghua and Berkeley and working as a chip R&D/design engineer in Silicon Valley. HyperStrong became one of China's top battery energy-storage system integrators (400+ projects, 70+ GWh in 30+ countries) and listed on the STAR Market in 2025. He now pushes a 'storage + X' strategy, including storage-plus-compute.
interesting_fact: In Sept 2026 HyperStrong broke ground in Baotou on an integrated storage-and-compute project with a 'token factory' (词元工厂): grid-side batteries co-sited with a distributed AI computing center selling metered AI compute, using its own solid-state transformer (HyperSST).
deep_cut_fact: Before energy storage he was a Silicon Valley chip R&D/design engineer ('from Tsinghua to Berkeley'); in Sept 2026 he was named one of the '2026 Beijing Role Models' (北京榜样) for August.
notes: Excellent fit for the energy x data-center theme (storage-compute 'token factory' in Baotou). HyperStrong has US offices (Chicago, Houston, San Francisco) and is shortlisted at the Energy Storage Awards in London on 19 Nov 2026, possible in-person angle. Contact is company-level only.

name: Feng Yongmao
current_role: Individual shareholder (5th largest, ~1.93% / 4.81M shares as of 30 Sep 2026) of Advanced Fiber Resources (Zhuhai), 300620.SZ; no board or management role
profile: Feng Yongmao (冯永茂) appears in AFR's filings only as a large private shareholder. AFR (光库科技), founded 2000 in Zhuhai and listed 2017, makes fiber-optic components and photonic chips (incl. thin-film lithium niobate modulators) for AI data centers, telecom, subsea cables and fiber lasers; it is controlled by state-owned Zhuhai Huafa. name: Farhad Ebrahimi
current_role: Private investor (Denver); former CEO and co-owner of Quark, Inc.; major holder of Royal Hawaiian Orchards and a First Solar investor
profile: Farhad 'Fred' Ebrahimi (87), an Iranian-born immigrant in Denver, joined desktop-publishing software maker Quark as CEO and co-owner in 1986 and later bought out co-founder Tim Gill; the family sold Quark to Platinum Equity in 2011. He then invested in Hawaii (owning ~80% of macadamia producer Royal Hawaiian Orchards by 2018) and in solar-panel maker First Solar.

Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/profile/farhad-ebrahimi/. Web-search budget ran out before checking Hawaii holdings/press routes.

name: Chi Fung Cheng
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Technology Officer and Director, Credo Technology Group (Nasdaq: CRDO)
profile: Chi Fung 'Lawrence' Cheng, 57, co-founded high-speed connectivity chipmaker Credo in 2008 after 11 years as an engineering director of analog design at Marvell, and has been CTO since. Credo's SerDes/DSP chips, retimers and 'ZeroFlap' active electrical cables connect servers and switches in AI data centers at up to 1.6T; it listed on Nasdaq in 2022. He holds roughly 4% of the company.
interesting_fact: Credo's active electrical cables (AECs) - copper cables with Credo DSPs built in - have become a key interconnect in AI clusters, with products spanning 32G to 200G per lane and 1.6T links.
deep_cut_fact: Before Marvell, Cheng spent 1994-1997 as a staff engineer at Actel Corporation, an FPGA/integrated-circuit maker, after earning an M.S. in electrical engineering at Purdue.
notes: Low-profile technical founder; CEO Bill Brennan is Credo's public face. IR contact is Dan O'Neil. Credo website blocked automated fetches (403), so no press email verified there.

name: Kirit Doshi
current_role: Minority shareholder (promoter-family member) of Waaree Energies Ltd, Mumbai
profile: Mumbai-based member of the Doshi family behind Waaree Energies, India's largest solar-module maker by capacity. Waaree began in 1990 under his brother Hitesh as a maker of thermal and pressure gauges for industrial boilers, moved into solar panels, and listed in October 2024 at a 70% premium to its IPO price; Kirit's minority stake made him a billionaire (Forbes, age 61).
interesting_fact: Waaree started out making thermal and pressure gauges for industrial boilers before becoming India's largest solar-module manufacturer, now with five module plants in India.
notes: Low-profile family shareholder; brother Hitesh Doshi (chairman) is Waaree's public face. Waaree's contact page lists the general company email waaree@waaree.com. Exact current executive title at Waaree not verified (web search budget exhausted); no deep-cut fact could be sourced.

name: Andrew Feldman
current_role: Co-founder, President and CEO, Cerebras Systems (Nasdaq: CBRS)
profile: Palo Alto-raised, Stanford BA/MBA serial founder who co-founded Cerebras in 2015-16 with his SeaMicro team to build the Wafer-Scale Engine, the largest chip ever made, for AI training and inference. Cerebras IPO'd on Nasdaq in May 2026 at $185/share, raising $5.55B and jumping ~68% on day one; he owns roughly 5% between stock and options.
interesting_fact: Cerebras' Wafer-Scale Engine uses an entire silicon wafer as one processor (WSE-3: 4 trillion transistors, 900,000 cores); in 2022 the Computer History Museum installed a permanent display of it as the first wafer-scale integration achieved in computing history.
deep_cut_fact: Data-center energy was his theme long before AI: his prior startup SeaMicro was 'founded to dramatically reduce the power consumed by servers' - its microservers used about a quarter of the power and a sixth of the space of conventional servers - and AMD bought it in 2012 for ~$334M.

public_contacts.value: pr@zmcommunications.com (ZM Communications, media contact on Cerebras press releases)

notes: Highly media-accessible and a frequent podcast guest; excellent fit for AI chips/inference and data-center power. PR agency contact dates from 2024 releases - check a recent Cerebras release for the current media contact. Personal X/LinkedIn not verified in this pass.

name: Wang Zhenggen
current_role: Director and General Manager, Suzhou Maxwell Technologies (迈为股份, SZSE: 300751)
profile: Wang Zhenggen (54) co-founded Suzhou Maxwell Technologies in 2010 with Zhou Jian; it listed in Shenzhen in 2018. Maxwell makes solar-cell production equipment (screen-printing, HJT and perovskite-silicon tandem lines) and has expanded into OLED/MicroLED laser tools and chip wafer-packaging equipment, selling into Thailand, Turkey and the US.
interesting_fact: Maxwell says it was the first company to localize complete solar-cell screen-printing lines and HJT cell lines in China, and its screen-printing lines have been No.1 by global market share every year 2018-2025; its tandem perovskite/silicon line targets >31% cell efficiency.
notes: Forbes profile: https://www.forbes.com/profile/wang-zhenggen/ (residence Suzhou). Co-founder Zhou Jian is chairman. Maxwell's IR site has an investor 'interactive platform' (SZSE Hudongyi) rather than a published IR email; the board-secretary email would be in its annual report. Semiconductor packaging tools give a chip/AI angle beyond solar.

name: Tang Xiaodong
current_role: Director and public-relations director, Bestechnic (BES, 恒玄科技), Shanghai (per 2020 IPO prospectus); co-controlling shareholder
profile: Tang Xiaodong (b. 1975, female) is one of Bestechnic's three co-controlling shareholders with her husband, chairman Liang Zhang, and vice chairman Zhao Guoguang. name: Jay Hyung Son
current_role: Co-founder and executive director, Innoscience (Suzhou) Technology (HKEX: 2577) - responsible for business development (per Dec 2024 prospectus)
profile: American semiconductor entrepreneur (age ~63) who co-founded Innoscience with chair Luo Weiwei; the two are its controlling shareholders. Innoscience is the world's largest GaN-dedicated chipmaker (8-inch GaN-on-silicon; ~30% global GaN power-device share in 2024), listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2024 and partnering with Nvidia on 800VDC power for AI data centers. current_role: Actual controller (controlling shareholder) of Anhui XDLK Microsystem (芯动联科, SSE STAR: 688582); not a current director or officer

Founded in 2012, XDLK listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in June 2023; he controls it via vehicles such as MEMSLink Corp. plus a ~1.3% direct stake.

profile: Yu Faxin (郁发新), a Zhejiang University aerospace-electronics professor since 2006, turned chip entrepreneur. name: Lucy Gou
current_role: Founder, Passes (creator monetization platform); founder, Backend Capital

Meta's 2025 $14.3B investment valuing Scale at $29B+ made her a billionaire; she now runs creator platform Passes and seed fund Backend Capital.

name: Jony Ive
current_role: Founder, LoveFrom (with Marc Newson); leads design across OpenAI after OpenAI acquired his device startup io (2025)
profile: British-American designer (b. 1967, Chingford) who as Apple's design chief shaped the iMac, iPod, iPhone and iPad before leaving in 2019 to found LoveFrom in San Francisco. Fit is AI hardware/design rather than energy. Fun aside: LoveFrom's bear mascot 'Montgomery' is named after Montgomery Street, SF.

current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, KP Group (KPI Green Energy, KP Energy, KP Green Engineering), Surat, Gujarat
profile: Dr. Faruk G. Patel founded KP Group in Surat in 1994 as a small logistics and construction venture and built it into a renewables conglomerate (solar, wind, hybrid, BESS, green hydrogen) with a 10.6+ GW portfolio. name: Mira Murati

profile: Albanian-born engineer (Colby BA, Dartmouth BEng) who worked on Tesla's Model X and at Leap Motion before joining OpenAI in 2018, rising to CTO and briefly interim CEO in Nov 2023. profile: Shahril Shamsuddin built Sapura Energy (formerly SapuraKencana, now renamed Vantris Energy) into one of Malaysia's largest offshore oil-and-gas service and drilling groups, and led the wider family conglomerate Sapura Group (energy, engineering, aviation, defence, property). name: Peter Smedvig

He took Smedvig ASA into offshore drilling (listed Oslo 1990, NYSE 1996), exited shipping (1996) and drilling (2006), and built the Smedvig Family Office (~US$2.4bn AUM), now owned by the 4th generation.

Goldman Sachs invested ~$40M in 2008; CS Wind now runs plants across Asia, Europe and the US, with day-to-day CEOs under him.

name: Ramachandra Galla
current_role: Founder Chairman, Amara Raja Group (Amara Raja Energy & Mobility; son Jayadev Galla is chairman & MD of the listed company)

Galla returned to Andhra Pradesh and at about 46-50 founded Amara Raja (1984-85), which grew into India's No. 2 lead-acid battery maker (Amaron, PowerZone) and now builds lithium-ion cells and packs at a 'Giga Corridor' in Telangana. The group marked its 40th foundation day in Dec 2025.
notes: Born c. 1938; alive status inferred from the group's leadership page listing him as Founder Chairman and an Oct 2024 lifetime-achievement award - not independently confirmed. Elderly and no longer on the listed company's board; son Jayadev Galla (ex-MP) is the practical interview route for batteries/energy storage. No published press email found.

name: Chen Haibo
current_role: Founder and head of DeepBlue Technology (DeepBlue AI, Shanghai)
profile: Chen Haibo founded Shanghai-based AI company DeepBlue Technology (est. 2014; site claims 2012), which grew from unattended retail systems (quiXmart, 'take-and-go' checkout, palm/face payment) into computer vision, autonomous 'Panda' smart buses and street sweepers, service robots and, recently, vertical LLMs and AI agents. DeepBlue reached unicorn status and says it has completed a shareholding reform and a Pre-IPO round.
interesting_fact: DeepBlue claims 50+ wins at top AI competitions (CVPR, ICCV, KDD, ACL), nearly 1,000 invention patents, and launched an enterprise 'AI agent work phone' built on Huawei Kirin/HarmonyOS.
